 Actor Kevin Pollak has recalled an unusual moment between Tom Cruise and Jack Nicholson during the filming of A Few Good Men, the 1992 courtroom drama directed by Rob Reiner. Speaking on the Still Here Hollywood podcast with Steve Kmetko earlier in the week, Pollak described how Cruise maintained his focus during an intense confrontation before punching Nicholson in the shoulder after the scene ended.
 Pollak, who also appeared in the film, recounted the incident during the climactic courtroom exchange between Cruise's character, Lt. Daniel Kaffee, and Nicholson's character, Col. Nathan Jessup. The scene features Kaffee challenging the commanding officer in a confrontation that became one of the film's defining moments.

 According to Pollak, Nicholson made an exaggerated facial expression while the camera captured the scene from the colonel's perspective. Cruise continued performing despite the unexpected distraction.

 Pollak described the moment on the podcast.
 "I remember there's one moment while shooting 'A Few Good Men,' the climactic scene of Tom and Jack going toe-to-toe. Kaffee against the colonel. When Tom's character, Kaffee, comes in for the kill. 'I want the truth.' Well, while he's coming in and the camera is next to Jack's face, shooting Jack's POV of Tom and Jack has to put his face as close as he can to lens," Pollak said.
 He explained that Nicholson's expression caught his attention as the confrontation unfolded, creating an unexpected challenge for Cruise while the cameras were rolling.

 "And Tom's coming in, camera shooting, and this is what Tom's looking at during the scene. Jack is doing this, making the most ridiculous clown face you've ever seen," Pollak said.
 Despite Nicholson's antics, Cruise completed the scene before reacting physically, according to Pollak. The two actors then laughed about the incident.
 "And Tom stayed in the pocket and finished the scene and then punched Jack Nicholson in the shoulder. Uh, and they both laughed. So, that was Jack and my experience," Pollak said.

 Anne Hathaway and Dakota Johnson Star in Thriller Verity 
 A Few Good Men follows Kaffee, a military lawyer played by Cruise, as he defends two U.S. Marines accused of murdering a fellow Marine at Guantánamo Bay. The case examines whether the defendants acted under an unauthorized disciplinary order known as a code red.
 Nicholson portrayed Jessup, whose testimony leads to the film's famous courtroom confrontation. Demi Moore played Lt. Cdr.
 JoAnne Galloway, Kaffee's colleague, while the cast also included Kevin Bacon, Kiefer Sutherland and J.T. Walsh.

 The film received four Academy Award nominations, including best picture, best supporting actor for Nicholson and best film editing.
 Pollak also discussed his experience working with Reiner, who died after the film's release, in an interview with People in June. He recalled the director's emphasis on enjoying the filmmaking process, even when working on an intense courtroom drama.
 "The big thing with Rob was just, if we're not having fun, there's no point in any of this," Pollak told People. "And he said that while we're doing a very intense courtroom drama, and it was a great lesson and a great way to work."

 Pollak also shared a memory from the production's time in Washington, D.C., where he and Reiner filmed exterior scenes. During a walk together, a passerby recognized the director and asked what project he was working on.
 Pollak recalled that Reiner gave an unexpected answer to avoid a lengthy conversation and allow them to continue walking.
 "One of my most enjoyable moments was [when] we shot a couple weeks in Washington D.C. to establish exteriors, and one night we were walking back from somewhere, just the two of us, and someone passed us and said, ‘Oh my God, Rob Reiner, how are you? Are you here working?' And he said, ‘Yeah.'

 He said, ‘What are you working on?' And he said, ‘The Godfather,'" Pollak told People.
 Pollak said he asked Reiner why he had named a different film, prompting an explanation of the director's strategy for ending the encounter quickly.
 "And the guy went, ‘Oh great.' He kept walking, and I said, ‘Why did you say The Godfather?' And he said, ‘Well, if I said A Few Good Men, it was a Broadway play, but if you didn't see the Broadway play, you don't know what the hell I'm talking about.
 So if I say The Godfather, we're done talking, and you and I can keep going with our lives.' I've used it ever since," Pollak said.
